newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering outperforms on dividend hopes.
newsitem.headline: Schering outperforms on dividend hopes.

text.p: Shares in German pharmaceutical group Schering AG outperformed on Thursday after company chairman Giuseppe Vita said the group might raise its dividend on 1996 results to a higher-than-expected two marks.
The stock was up two marks, or 1.7 percent, at 119.10 marks in early bourse trade, while the 30-share DAX index was up 9.26 points or 0.35 percent at 2,668.23 points at 0900 GMT.

Vita told German television on Wednesday evening that the company was expecting its profits to rise 30 percent in 1996 and that sales would be up around 11 percent -- making a two-mark dividend possible.
Schering last year paid out 1.55 marks per share.
"Two marks is definitely higher than most people expected," said Bank Julis Baer analyst Martin Wirth.
"I had expected 1.70 marks and the consenus appeared to be about the 1.70 to 1.80 mark level."
Bank Julius Baer has had a buy recommendation on Schering since it reported unexpectedly strong first-half earnings in August and will maintain it, Wirth said.

"I think Schering is one of the cheapest pharma shares in Germany. It has had several problems with its bottom line in the past -- due to one-offs and to currency problems -- but the fundamentals are good," he added.
